channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: WATCH: Authorities: Fatal alligator attack in Winter Garden, Florida
item.description: Police say the man was fishing along the shoreline at a park when he was attacked and killed by an alligator.

item.title: Bend, Oregon, shooting: Suspect ID'd, had attended elementary school, police say
item.description: Three children and one teacher are dead after a shooter forced his way into a Bend, Oregon, elementary school and opened fire, authorities said.

item.title: Bipartisan group of senators want answers on Starlink disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: The lawmakers say American personnel were endangered in attacks on Ukraine.

item.title: Georgia's Senate and governor races test Trump's political influence
item.description: Trump plays a significant role in Georgia's races, with Democrats working to tie their GOP opponents to Trump’s unpopular policies on the economy and war with Iran.

item.title: WATCH: Hero who stopped Oregon elementary school shooting suspect identified
item.description: ABC News contributor Don Mihalek discusses the bystander credited with stopping the suspected gunman and ongoing investigations.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: Judge tosses indictment against actor Timothy Busfield
item.description: A New Mexico judge has dismissed an indictment against actor and director Timothy Busfield on four counts of sexual contact of a minor.

item.title: Family 'broken and lost' after five-year-old boy killed in school shooting
item.description: The family of a five-year-old boy killed in a school shooting in Oregon say they are "broken and lost".

item.title: 4,400 measles cases reported in US as CDC to send 'disease detective' to Pennsylvania
item.description: More than 4,400 measles cases have been reported in the U.S. as the CDC says it plans to send a "disease detective" to Pennsylvania.

item.title: Zelensky turns to Europe for backing as ties with Trump deteriorate
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky turned to his European allies on Friday, asking Brussels for an additional €70 billion to fund the war against Russia next year. Zelensky's relationship with US President Donald Trump deteriorated after the US eased sanctions on Moscow as part of a diesel-supply deal.

item.title: KENYA CONFIRMS THIRD EBOLA CASE
item.description: In tonight's programme, Kenya confirms a third case of Ebola, a relative of a man who died earlier this month after travelling from DR Congo. Also,Cameroonian journalist Ambe Macmillan is recovering in hospital after being shot in the legs by gunmen in Bamenda. And we meet Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama... And finally, we meet Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama, who digs deep into his country's colonial and industrial past to lay new creative foundations for generations to come.

item.title: Man convicted of arson attacks against Keir Starmer deported from UK
item.description: A man convicted of arson attacks targeting Sir Keir Starmer has been deported, the Home Office said.

item.title: 'Finish what we started': After student protests, France braces for return of the Yellow Vests
item.description: An online movement against rising fuel prices has gained momentum ahead of planned nationwide demonstrations on October 17 with former Yellow Vest figures set to join the protests in support of high-school students. Some are drawing parallels between the latest action and the 2018 cost-of-living protests that rattled President Emmanuel Macron's first term in office.

item.title: Clashes grip Tirana as Albanian PM blames 'foreign hands' for mounting unrest
item.description: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama on Friday blamed the involvement of “foreign hands” for escalating protests, which he said are aimed at hindering Albania's bid to join the European Union. Thousands of demonstrators have taken to the streets of Albania's capital since Tuesday, demanding Rama’s resignation and denouncing university conditions and high tuition fees.

item.title: How Elon Musk is bankrolling GOP’s hopes in Texas Senate race
item.description: New campaign finance filings show the major role billionaire Elon Musk is playing in bankrolling GOP efforts against Democrat James Talarico in Texas.

item.title: Trump Vs Zelensky, From the Screen to the Streets, Gen Z protests from Paris to Dehli
item.description: In India, the Cockroach movement felt the crushing boot of the state this week. Thousands of Gen Z protesters were rounded up and detained in sports stadiums and community halls turned into makeshift detention centres, while the movement’s founder, Abhijeet Dipke, was arrested on arrival. A mass demonstration over alleged voter fraud was effectively crushed before it could begin.And Abdijeet has been detained again todayNarendra Modi’s government says the measures were necessary to protect civilians in the capital. But he now faces accusations of choosing repression over democracy, with the UN Human Rights Office urging authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly. It’s been a week of blame games and accusations of betrayal in Ukraine with President Zelensky speaking of his personal hurt at President Trump’s decision to make a diesel deal with the Kremlin ahead of the US Mid term elections calling it “weak”, suggesting Trump had chosen, “the other side”. item.title: 'US tilting toward Russia: Europeans are standing more and more solidly with Zelensky'
item.description: As transatlantic relations confront renewed geopolitical uncertainty, former Estonian President Toomas Hendrik Ilves delivers a pointed assessment of Washington's shifting approach to Russia's war on Ukraine and the profound implications for European security. At the heart of his analysis lies a fundamental question: can Europe develop the political unity, strategic independence and military capabilities necessary to defend its interests in an increasingly unpredictable international order? Ilves response: "If there's any time for Europe to begin to act as Europe and not as being strictly self-interested, then this is the time for it."

item.title: WATCH: Nat Geo's 'Moment on the Earth' spotlights the wonders of elephants
item.description: National Geographic shares a closer look at elephants, including how they can eat up to 18 hours a day and even use their trunks to "hug." "Secrets of the Elephants" is streaming now.

item.title: Hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia – OB-GYNS set new rules for menopause treatment
item.description: For the first time since 2014, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has updated its guidelines for the treatment of symptoms commonly associated with menopause.

item.title: Under-fire White House spokesperson leaves after a week
item.description: Katie Zacharia has left her role as White House press secretary a week after being appointed.

item.title: Four dead as Istanbul suffers worst floods in 80 years
item.description: At least four people have died after Istanbul suffered its worst floods in more than 80 years, Turkish officials have said.

item.title: Amid talk of public execution, public opinion on death penalty is split
item.description: A majority of Americans support the death penalty for people convicted of murder, but support becomes more divided when questions vary.

item.title: Sally Rooney's books no longer sold in UK over support for banned pro-Palestinian group
item.description: Irish novelist Sally ⁠Rooney's books will ​no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties ​to support Palestine Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and her publisher said on Wednesday. The bestselling author, known for novels including "Normal People" and "Conversations with ​Friends", has ‌been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after ⁠it was proscribed by the British government under terrorism laws last year.

item.title: Argentine demonstration over education cuts ends in clashes
item.description: Argentine demonstrators clashed with police on Thursday at a major protest in Buenos Aires over budget-slashing President Javier Milei's higher education spending. The main demonstration outside parliament by thousands of university students and staff, trade unionists and opposition activists remained peaceful. But dozens of mostly hooded demonstrators who broke away from the crowd lobbed stones and other projectiles at the police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons.

item.title: Iran live updates: Trump admin prepares options, including 'mother of all bombs'
item.description: A dozen people were killed Saturday during a "brutal" attack at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said.

item.title: Embattled new White House Press Secretary Zacharia 'let go' from her role
item.description: A White House Press official said Friday that Secretary ​Katie Zacharia was "let go" from her role after US President Donald Trump signaled she was on her way out, a week after he picked her for the post. Zacharia's credentials as an attorney had come under scrutiny and she admitted to not having passed the bar in an interview with Fox News on Thursday.

item.title: India detains top 'cockroach' leader as hundreds protest in capital
item.description: Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Abhijeet Dipke on Friday ahead of fresh protests demanding the removal of the country's election chief, the youth-led movement said in a social media post. Dipke, 31, was detained shortly before a rally called by the online movement in the heart of New Delhi where hundreds of protesters marched on Friday evening, despite heavy security measures. FRANCE 24's Navodita Kumari reports from New Delhi, India.

item.title: Ex-soap star who conned would-be models in £13m scam jailed after fleeing UK
item.description: A former soap opera star has been jailed for nine years after fleeing the UK for Spain to avoid facing trial for allegedly conning would-be models out of more than £13m.

item.title: Zelensky hails "real leaders" in Europe, blasts Trump's diesel deal with Russia
item.description: Ukrainian ​President Volodymyr Zelensky took aim on Friday at US President Donald Trump's diesel deal with Russia and welcomed the prospect of European allies stepping up their role in talks, calling Moscow's stance a "parody" of peace negotiations. At a European Union summit in Brussels, Zelenskiy said Russia did not want peace. He added that Ukraine was still experiencing disruptions to the SpaceX Starshield satellite system. FRANCE 24's Europe Editor Armen Georgian reports from Brussels.

item.title: France braces for massive protests: Yellow Vests to join students on Saturday
item.description: After weeks of student protests, France is set to be swept by broader, nationwide demonstrations on Saturday. The country's Yellow Vest movement – which eight years ago staged street protests against President Emmanuel Macron – has appealed to teachers, workers, pensioners and farmers, as well as students, in an online call spread through social media. The prospect of the two movements merging poses a big challenge to the government, as FRANCE 24’s Shirli Sitbon reports.

item.title: Italy prolongs Schengen suspension with Spain, talks loom
item.description: Italy has extended by another week ​its suspension of the European Union's border-free travel arrangements with Spain over a surge in migrant arrivals in Ceuta in late July, ​an ‌Italian government source said on Friday. A ⁠Spanish government spokesperson said the interior ministers of both countries would work over ‌the coming week on lifting the border controls.

item.title: REPLAY: Ukraine's Zelensky holds presser in Brussels
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Friday urged European leaders to maintain their support for Kyiv and warned against easing sanctions on Russia. Speaking to reporters at the European summit in Brussels, Zelensky said that ending the war remained Ukraine’s priority but accused Russian President Vladimir Putin of having no genuine interest in negotiations. He also criticised a US deal involving Russian diesel, arguing that easing restrictions could allow Moscow to reap financial benefits and pave the way for broader sanctions relief. Watch the replay.

item.title: Indonesia's forest fires spark public health crisis across Southeast Asia
item.description: Massive wildfires in Indonesia show no sign of letting up. The environmental disaster is turning into a pollution crisis across Southeast Asia, as toxic haze from the blazes spread to neighbouring countries.

item.title: The risks faced by women migrants in Europe
item.description: This October marks 10 years since French police dismantled the notorious Calais "Jungle" camp. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin returns to the region to explore what has changed for migrants over the past decade. She joins Annette Young and Dr Marissa Quie of Cambridge University to discuss migration routes and their growing role in European political debate.

item.title: US journalist injured during Israeli settler attack on West Bank olive harvest
item.description: About 80 Israeli settlers set fire to olive trees and threw stones at Palestinians in a West Bank village Friday, injuring at least two people, including a US photojournalist with The Washington Post. The coordinated attack came as violence by settlers is on the rise during the olive harvest in the occupied Palestinian territory.

item.title: Ibrahim Mahama's abundant artistic harvest
item.description: His monumental installations excavate Ghana's past and build firm foundations for the country’s artistic future. Ibrahim Mahama has represented his country at the Venice Biennale and established three cultural hubs in northern Ghana, nurturing creative communities for generations to come.

item.title: Trump administration accused of fast-tracking migrant children's asylum cases
item.description: Immigrant advocacy groups have sued the Trump administration to stop what they call a "cruel and unlawful scheme" to fast-track migrant children's asylum cases.

item.title: Tiger victim's medical records may have been improperly accessed
item.description: NHS staff may have improperly accessed information about a man killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.

item.title: WATCH: Aboard USS George Washington as tensions rise in the Middle East
item.description: ABC News is aboard the USS George Washington near the Strait of Hormuz with rare front-line access as President Donald Trump weighs expanded operations against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

item.title: South African rugby player Hyron ​Andrews dies in France ahead of Champions Cup debut
item.description: Hyron ​Andrews, a 31-year-old rugby player for the Lions team, was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday, the day before the South African club ​are due to play La Rochelle in the Champions Cup. The match will go ahead in his honour, his team said.

item.title: Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating protests
item.description: Protests have intensified over a review of voter lists that critics say is politically motivated and threatens to disenfranchise voters. The Election Commission and Modi's administration deny these allegations.

item.title: Ethiopia announces interim government in Tigray, aims for polls in six months
item.description: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday announced the appointment of an interim administration to prepare elections in the northern Tigray region previously controlled by the Tigray People's Liberation Front that has clashed with government forces since September. The recent conflict revived a war that killed hundreds of thousands between 2020 and 2022.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates mass in hospital while recovering from lung cancer operation
item.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated a mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital Friday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung, photos released by the Vatican showed. Doctors said his recovery was progressing normally but that further tests would show whether the cancer had spread.

item.title: 'America, with this president, is not our ally. Trump is a liar': French MEP Bernard Guetta
item.description: Our guest is veteran French journalist and commentator Bernard Guetta, who is a Member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group. He tells the programme that Donald Trump is "a liar, because he tried to tell the American people that Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance were responsible for the price of diesel. This is a pure lie. He (Trump) is responsible because he started the war with Iran." Guetta goes on to say that "without American intelligence sharing, Ukraine is weaker and weaker. That's terrible, to see the president of the United States giving a hand to Putin against Ukraine."

item.title: 'Thanks a lot, Trump': Wyoming conservatives divided ahead of US midterms
item.description: Famous for its cowboy culture, Wyoming is the least populated, the most rural and the most conservative of all the US states. With two weeks to go until the midterm elections, our reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau travelled across this Republican stronghold and found that the party of US President Donald Trump is deeply divided in the Cowboy State.

item.title: What the Pope said to Putin in call days after lung cancer surgery
item.description: The Pope spoke to Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday and urged a truce with Ukraine as he continued his recovery from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said.

item.title: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia says she did not pass bar exam
item.description: Zacharia has described herself as a lawyer; Trump called her "an attorney."

item.title: WATCH: Elon Musk unveils Tesla's new Roadster, and it can fly
item.description: Using SpaceX rocket technology, the sports car climbed a curved ramp and hurled itself to a controlled landing.

item.title: Drugs fuelling 'horrific' events seen in Waterford, says Irish justice minister
item.description: People who take illegal drugs are "supporting the horrific events we saw in Waterford", Irish justice minister Jim O'Callaghan has said.

item.title: Madeleine McCann prime suspect could face new rape trial
item.description: The prime suspect in the Madeleine McCann case could face a new rape trial after German prosecutors launched a legal bid to overturn his acquittal on a string of sex charges, unrelated to the missing British girl.

item.title: CDC lags in hiring behind other health agencies after DOGE cuts, union says
item.description: More than a year after cutting 30% of its workforce and disrupting dozens of public health programs, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is lagging in hiring.

item.title: Nicolas Maduro and wife deny new torture charges as 'false accusations'
item.description: Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro has rejected newly unsealed torture allegations against him and his wife as "false accusations".

item.title: British man fined for causing death of his two-year-old son in Cyprus
item.description: A British father has been fined €3,000 (£2,500) for causing the death of his two-year-old son who fell from the fourth floor of a hotel in Cyprus.

item.title: WATCH: Rhode Island farmer sets new record for world's biggest pumpkin
item.description: David Muir reports on the new world record for heaviest pumpkin, which weighs 3,156 pounds – smashing the previous record of 2,856 pounds set merely a week ago.

item.title: WATCH: Seahawks, Broncos face off in Thursday night NFL matchup
item.description: ESPN’s Omar Ruiz previews the Seahawks-Broncos showdown in Denver, including how Seattle’s top-ranked defense could challenge Bo Nix and whether Sam Darnold can bounce back after two interceptions.

item.title: Trump claims executive privilege to keep Kennedy Center conversations secret
item.description: A White House lawyer said Trump's executive privilege would also cover his conversations with advisers who don't serve in government.

item.title: WATCH: Rising number of young adults living with parents
item.description: ABC News’ Juju Chang reports on the growing trend of “boomerang kids” returning to live with their parents amid housing costs and financial concerns.

item.title: 19 injured after Channel Tunnel collision between bus and train
item.description: Nineteen people have been injured after a collision between a bus and a train on the French side of the Channel Tunnel.

item.title: WATCH: DIY Halloween costumes for this year’s viral trends
item.description: Lori Bergamotto shares easy, last-minute DIY Halloween costume ideas inspired by the people and pop culture moments that made headlines this year.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir hears from Georgia firefighters who helped deliver 15 puppies
item.description: Firefighters in Cobb County answered an emergency call to help a veterinary hospital deliver 15 puppies after a rescue dog came to the local animal hospital.

item.title: Norwegian teenage hitman who flew to UK to commit murder jailed
item.description: A Norwegian teenager who flew to the UK to carry out murder for an Iran-backed gang has been jailed for 20 years.

item.title: WATCH: Aggressive great white shark seen off Southern California coast
item.description: Experts say the shark could be hunting for seals.

item.title: School owner arrested after dozens of children killed in roof collapse
item.description: At least 34 children and a teacher have died after the roof of a private school collapsed in Pakistan.

item.title: WATCH: Measles, GLP-1s and anti-aging: How to protect your health
item.description: Dr. Raj Panjabi discusses the resurgence of measles, the potential health benefits of GLP-1 drugs and what we can do now to prevent disease and live longer.

item.title: WATCH: How to navigate rising prices this holiday season
item.description: ABC News’ Elizabeth Schulze reports on what to know about the latest inflation report and prices this coming holiday season.

item.title: Man and woman arrested after two adults and two children killed in house fire
item.description: Two people have been arrested over the deaths of two adults and two children in a suspected arson attack on a house in Ireland.
